Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
HIP JOINT WITH LOCK FOR ORTHOSIS 

( First Revision ) 



1. Scope — Prescribes dimensional and other requirements of hip joint with lock for steel orthopaedic 
calipers and barces. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

Fig. 1 HIP JOINT WITH LOCK FOR STEEL ORTHOPAEDIC CALIPER AND BRACES 

3. Material — Carbon steel conforming to Designation 30C8 or 35C4 of IS : 1570 (Part 2)-1979 
'Schedules for wrought steels: Part 2 Carbon steels ( unalloyed steels) {first revision Y. 

4. Workmanship and Finish — The male and female parts of the joints shall be accurately and 
cleanly machined and the joint faces shall be finished clean and free from toolmarks. The male part 
shall be made to give a close running fit with the female joint member. The parts after assembly shall 
give a smooth jerk-free movement while flexing the joint. The outside surfaces of the joint and the 
shanks shall be free from forging scale. AH sharp edges and corners shall be rounded. There shall be 
no surface flaws and cracks on the finished components. All surfaces shall be finished smooth. 
Fabrications by welding or brazing shall not be allowed. There shall not be any frictional, jerky or 
mediolateral movement at the joints. 

5. Marking — The joint shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) Size of the joint ( see Fig. 1 ),
